doc.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022

title: Rhythm section trust and relying on intuition
summary: Galper says not to bring paper to the bandstand, praises bassist Tony Marino and others who follow him anywhere, and argues intuition is never wrong.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So how does your trio bass player learn some of these re-harmonized tunes? Do you write a chord chart for him?
Yes. But don’t bring it to the bandstand.
You don’t bring it to what?
You don’t bring any paper to the bandstand.

Not good. It doesn’t look good. You’ve got to get it memorized. And Tony [Marino], Tony has, I’ve been playing with Tony for decades. He’s a consum — he’s a symphony master bassist. It doesn’t make any — I can get lost and he’ll just follow me. It doesn’t make any difference to him or to me, whichever way we go Tony is going to be there. It just never fails. He’ll just go — like I said I have a short term memory problem. Sometimes, like this Saturday we were playing a song and I got distracted and I totally lost the key center in the song. I didn’t — Tony was soloing and I didn’t know what tune we were playing or what key we were in, couldn’t tell. So that’s — hey welcome to being 84 you know. But luckily it doesn’t happen too much. It happens mostly when I’m talking you know. But Tony and Billy [Mintz], they just follow me anywhere I go. It doesn’t make any difference what I do they just follow me. They’re great. And it was the same way with Jeff Johnson and John Bishop. They were really crazy enough to follow me.
I wonder if they’re thinking how are we going to get out of this now. How is this going to resolve itself.

Thinking is no good. Thinking doesn’t work. Thinking is slow. The only thing that could make the decisions about note choice is the limbic system. Down there decisions are made almost at the speed of light. And you’re not even aware of it. I trust my intuition a hell of a lot more than my intellect. A hell of a lot more. It’s never wrong. Never. You know when you’re leaving the house and your intuition tells you — and it’s sunny outside and your intuition tells you I should bring an umbrella out. Something pops up from real deep down below because your body is an antenna and it’s monitoring the environment 24/7 okay. It’s picked some kind of information, maybe a slight change upwards in humidity or something that you didn’t notice, but it’s beautiful sunlight outside and you say naa, I don’t need it. And you get out there and next thing you know you’re in a rainstorm. It’s never wrong, your intuition. Never. But you have to trust it. That’s the tool we use. That’s one of the things we are training as we learn how to play is our intuition. It never is never wrong.
